mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which should positively impact corporate earnings and drive up stock prices, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 20-day horizon in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate suggests easier monetary policy, which can stimulate investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases by 0.5% in the last month
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate decreases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the triggered instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate revenues, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate is below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests higher economic activity, which can lead to improved corporate performance and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates increased construction activity and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by 5% in the last month
failure_condition: If housing starts increase by 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 100,000 in the last month
failure_condition: If payroll employment increases by 100,000 but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low inflation (CPIAUCSL) and low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a favorable economic environment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both CPIAUCSL is below 250 and UNRATE is below 4%, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, which can boost corporate revenues and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by 5% in the last month
failure_condition: If retail sales increase by 5% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
